summary: Revision 1 of 3: adds only the opt-in focus streak; the programmatic trigger belongs to a later revision and is not built here. One optional field joins the already-exported custom-props object, so useZestConfig's existing provider -> semantic -> local deep merge carries it through: no new export, no barrel change, no context, no dependency, and a button that omits the field renders and behaves exactly as today. The effect is pure CSS, with no React state, listeners or timers. A regular button gets a modifier class and a pseudo-element streak clipped by the button's existing position:relative, overflow:hidden and 8px radius. A split button gets the same modifier class on the existing split wrapper, which gains position:relative plus the existing force-light/force-dark theme class and small style/variant marker classes; the band is clipped by the overlay's own border-radius rather than by wrapper overflow, deliberately, so neither segment's outer focus ring is cut (R5). The overlay is driven by :has(:focus-visible) on the wrapper, so keyboard focus on either segment plays one whole-control sweep and a mouse click plays none; the wrapper's opted-in class also switches off the chevron's mount streak through a descendant rule, with no change to ZestDropdownMenu. The band is a diagonal ~45-degree gradient that travels top-right to bottom-left in ~0.6s, one sweep, ending transparent. Colour is derived from currentColor for the regular button (white on solid matches the existing chevron look; the accent colour on outline/text/dashed stays visible per style, variant and forced theme) and from a dedicated custom property chosen by style+variant+theme markers for the split overlay. Reduced motion disables both. Cost: when off there is no extra DOM and no CSS match, so behaviour and resource use are unchanged; when on the work is one pseudo-element layered paint animation, with no layout shift and no network, storage or startup cost. No dependency or build-output change (the project has no .size-limit.json; the stylesheet grows by a few hundred bytes).

reuses: the existing button class (position:relative, overflow:hidden, border-radius var(--zest-radius-md)) for the regular-button clip
the existing split wrapper and its ZestDropdownMenu chevron trigger
the existing force-light/force-dark theme classes and the --zest-color-*-bg/--zest-color-*-border variables for theme-aware band colour
the existing chevron mount-streak technique (gradient plus background-position keyframes) and the existing prefers-reduced-motion block
the existing color-mix usage with a static fallback for tolerance in older browsers
the existing useZestConfig provider/semantic/local merge so the new field needs no new context or hook
the existing CSS Modules injection and the Jest pattern of parsing the CSS module source for selector assertions
adds: An optional focus-sheen boolean field (default off) in UI/ZestButton.tsx on the already-exported custom-props interface; no new export, no barrel change, no dependency.
Focus-streak CSS rules, per-style and per-theme colour rules, the sweep keyframes, and split-wrapper positioning/theme marker rules added inside Styles/ZestButton.module.css.
New behavioural tests in __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx and characterisation tests in __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheenCharacterization.test.tsx (both in scope).

A new guide at docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md plus edits to documentation/api.md, documentation/features.md, documentation/examples.md, documentation/configuration.md and README.md (all in scope).

additions.title: Turn the focus streak off for reduced motion
additions.why: People who ask their device to reduce motion should not get a sweeping band.
acceptance: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, keyboard-focusing an opted-in regular or split button plays no streak and leaves no visible band.
Without that preference the streak still plays, for both regular and split buttons.

additions.title: Suppress the chevron mount streak when the focus streak is enabled
additions.why: Two streaks on one split control would collide and look like a glitch.
acceptance: An opted-in split button shows no chevron mount streak on first paint, on any button style, variant or theme.
A split button that is not opted in keeps its chevron mount streak exactly as today.

additions.title: Characterisation tests for the existing button appearance and chevron streak
additions.why: The shared stylesheet is being edited, so the behaviour already shipped is pinned before the change.
acceptance: Tests record the current class list of a plain regular button and of a split wrapper/button and pass before the change.
Tests record the existing chevron mount-streak rule and focus-ring rule and still pass after the change.
A button that does not pass the new option renders no sheen class and keeps the same DOM and behaviour.

additions.title: Document the focus streak on every page readers use
additions.why: A new prop that cannot be found is a feature nobody can use.
acceptance: documentation/api.md lists the new custom-props field with its default and both regular and split usage.
documentation/features.md and documentation/examples.md show the option on a regular button and a split button.
documentation/configuration.md notes that the provider's defaultProps can set it app-wide, and README links to the new guide.
The new docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md explains keyboard-only focus, clipping, colours per style/theme and reduced motion.
